newsitem.title: GERMANY: No German decision yet on debt conversion to Euro.
newsitem.headline: No German decision yet on debt conversion to Euro.

text.p: Germany has not yet decided when it will convert its existing mark-denominated government bonds into euros, a finance ministry official said on Thursday.
Finance ministry official Michael Roeskau told a conference on legislative issues relating to monetary union that "there has unfortunately been no agreement on this (debt conversion)."
"But we are certain we will be able to reach a decision and that it will be possible to convert existing debt to euros."
As of January 1, 1999, all new German government debt will be denominated in euros, but there is no obligation to convert existing debt issues on that date.
France has already said it will convert its existing debt at the start of monetary union. There has been pressure on Germany to do the same to keep its capital markets competitive.
